ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the line $l_{1}: y=x+3$ and the line $l_{2}: y=kx+b$ intersect at a point in the same Cartesian coordinate system. What is the solution set of the inequality $x+3<kx+b$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the line $l_{1}: y=x+3$ intersects with the line $l_{2}: y=kx+b$ at the point $(-1,2)$, \\
it follows that when $x<-1$, $x+3<kx+b$, \\
thus, the solution set for the inequality $x+3<kx+b$ with respect to $x$ is $x<-1$. \\
Therefore, the answer is $\boxed{x<-1}$.
